description:
You are the Chief Compliance Officer at Meridian Life Insurance Group, a $4.2B multi-line insurance carrier regulated by state departments of insurance in 38 states and subject to NAIC Model Audit Rule (MAR) requirements. It is the start of Q1, which means you must execute the annual information security policy review cycle as required by your information security program charter.

Your board-approved Information Security Policy Framework requires that all security policies be reviewed annually and assigned current statuses. Additionally, systems found to be non-compliant with existing policies must have formal exception records created with board-level visibility.

Complete ALL of the following in Eramba (credentials at /home/ga/eramba/credentials.txt):

1. Create at least 5 new security policies covering distinct information security domains not already covered by existing policies (the Acceptable Use Policy and Password Management Policy already exist). Your new policies must include at least: one policy with status 'Approved' covering data governance/classification, one policy with status 'Approved' covering access management, one policy with status 'Draft' covering business continuity/disaster recovery, one policy with status 'Draft' covering cryptography and key management, and one additional policy of your choice with any appropriate status. Having at least 2 Approved and 2 Draft policies is required.

2. Register at least 3 IT assets representing critical systems at Meridian Life (e.g., Policy Administration System, Customer Portal, Claims Processing Platform, Enterprise Data Warehouse, Actuarial Modeling Workstation). These assets represent the systems the policies govern.

3. Create at least 3 policy exceptions documenting systems that are currently non-compliant with one or more of your policies, with appropriate expiration dates set. Examples: legacy claims processing system exempt from encryption policy, actuarial workstation running unsupported OS pending hardware refresh, partner integration server exempt from MFA requirement.

4. Create a project with 'Policy' or 'Audit' in the title to track the annual review cycle activities (e.g., 'Annual Information Security Policy Review Cycle 2025' or 'Q1 Compliance Audit and Policy Refresh').

5. Update the status of at least one of the two pre-existing policies ('Acceptable Use Policy' or 'Password Management Policy') — for example, change the Acceptable Use Policy to reflect that it is currently under review by setting an updated description or any available field that reflects the review process. (If Eramba does not have an 'Under Review' status, you may re-save the policy with a minor description update to show the policy was reviewed.)
